narrativeSummary: May 18 was a bond market story. The 10Y Treasury yield surging above 4.60% to its highest level since January 2025 — and the 30Y hitting 5.134%, the highest since 2007 — overwhelmed every other market signal. The proximate cause was the compounding effect of two back-to-back inflation surprises: the April CPI at 3.8% (released May 12) and the April PPI data released Friday, both of which showed energy prices from the Iran war bleeding into core inflation metrics. Trading Economics confirmed traders have 'fully ruled out any Federal Reserve rate cuts this year' while 'increasing bets on a potential rate hike before year-end.' For the Nasdaq, which carries high-multiple AI names sensitive to discount rate moves, this was a painful session: tech dropped 1.1% intraday, NVDA fell 4.4% ahead of its Wednesday earnings, Seagate -7% on Samsung strike contagion. The lone bright spots arrived in waves. First: Trump announced he was delaying a military strike on Iran (scheduled for Tuesday) because 'serious negotiations are now taking place' — Brent had topped $110 intraday, but reversed sharply to close near $108-109. Iran confirmed it conveyed amended terms via Pakistani mediators. The ceasefire is fraying but the diplomatic track is not dead. Second: a federal jury dismissed Musk's lawsuit against OpenAI in under two hours, finding the claims fell outside the statute of limitations — a verdict that clears the most consequential legal overhang on OpenAI's path to IPO. The Musk verdict, combined with SpaceX's imminent prospectus disclosure and the Cerebras precedent, sets up what Benzinga called 'the most consequential back-to-back capital markets period in the history of the technology sector.' Third: the Dow itself — up 0.32% and the only major index in the green — told the rotation story: defensives (healthcare, staples, financials) absorbing the tech selloff. Samsung Electronics's 47,000-worker strike threat is the session's sleeper risk: if it materialises, memory supply chains tighten further just as Nvidia needs Blackwell chips for its May 20 report.
macroStressSubtext: 10Y 4.63% 52-week high + 30Y 5.134% 2007 high + rate hike re-priced. MSI jumps 16pts from Elevated to High. Iran attack delayed but not cancelled.
rateCurveRead: The curve sold off dramatically on May 18, extending a two-session bear-steepener triggered by the CPI 3.8% print last Tuesday and the PPI data on Friday. The 10Y hit 4.63% — its highest since January 2025 — representing a 25bp move from May 14's 4.38%, one of the fastest 10Y repricing events of the year. The 30Y reached 5.134% — highest since 2007 and the first time since the 2022-23 rate cycle that the 30Y has spent multiple sessions above 5.10%. The 2Y rose to 4.05%, now above 4% for the first time this cycle, confirming that near-term cut expectations have been fully priced out. Trading Economics: traders 'completely rule out any Fed rate cuts this year.' The 2/10 spread compressed to +58bps from +46bps as the long end moved faster than the short end — a classically stagflationary signal where growth concerns anchor the short end but inflation fears push the long end higher. Warsh June 17 inaugural meeting is now widely expected to be a hold with hawkish tone. Source: Trading Economics (10Y 4.63%), TheStreet (30Y 5.134%); H.15 official pending.

The three dominant outflows are long-duration bonds (-$2.3B), semiconductors (-$2.1B), and technology (-$1.4B). The Dow's green finish on defensive rotation confirms the same pattern in equity space. The session's most significant signal is the combined weight of the bear-steepener and the Iran delay: the bond market is telling you inflation is structural and the Fed will need to act, while the equity market is choosing to believe the Iran diplomatic track and position for Nvidia Wednesday rather than price in the full rate shock.

drivers.detail: The 10Y Treasury reached 4.63% on Monday — its highest level since January 2025 — completing a 25bp move in 4 sessions from May 14's 4.38%. The 30Y hit 5.134%, its highest since 2007. The 2Y crossed 4.00% for the first time this cycle. Trading Economics confirmed traders have 'completely ruled out any Federal Reserve rate cuts this year' while 'increasing bets on a potential rate hike before year-end.' The proximate cause: April CPI 3.8% (released May 12) and PPI data (released May 15) both showed Iran's energy shock bleeding into core inflation. RSM's Brusuelas had predicted CPI heading to 4% — the bond market is now pricing that scenario. Warsh inherits the worst inflation backdrop in 3 years at his first FOMC meeting June 17. fedTransitionRisk raised to 82 — highest since it was introduced as an indicator. realWageYoY deteriorated to -1.3%.

drivers.name: Trump Delays Iran Attack Scheduled for Tuesday — 'Serious Negotiations Now Taking Place'
drivers.linked: Brent, WTI, OGPI, Iran, Hormuz, hormuzclosurePct
drivers.source: Yahoo Finance live blog, TheStreet, CNN
drivers.detail: Brent topped $110 intraday — the highest level in weeks — as Trump warned Iran that 'the clock is ticking' and they had 'better get moving, FAST, or there won't be anything left of them.' A rally in oil prices had already stoked inflation jitters before the open. Then Trump announced he was delaying a military strike that had been scheduled for Tuesday, saying 'serious negotiations are now taking place.' Oil retreated sharply on the delay announcement. Iran confirmed it conveyed another amended set of terms via Pakistani mediators. Tehran said it is 'focused entirely on an agreement to end the war and has not yet discussed any details regarding nuclear matters.' A drone strike near UAE's sole nuclear power plant over the weekend (no injuries, no radiological release) added to the region's instability. Hormuz physically remains at 4% normal flow.

drivers.name: Musk Loses OpenAI Trial in Under 2 Hours — $150B Claims Dismissed, OpenAI $1T IPO Path Clear
drivers.linked: OpenAI IPO, MSFT, SpaceX, AI IPO wave, Altman
drivers.detail: A federal jury in Oakland dismissed all of Elon Musk's claims against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman in under two hours of deliberation. The verdict: Musk's claims fell outside the 3-year statute of limitations. Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers adopted the verdict immediately. Musk sought $150B in damages, removal of Altman and Brockman, and dismantling of OpenAI's for-profit structure. None were granted. Microsoft's $228.3B OpenAI stake (8% of MSFT market cap) preserved. OpenAI raised $122B at $852B valuation in March 2026, generating ~$2B/month revenue, targeting $1T IPO. SpaceX prospectus expected this week (Nasdaq June 12 target). Benzinga: 'The verdict arrives at exactly the right moment for OpenAI's capital markets ambitions.' Musk vows appeal and called it a 'calendar technicality.'

drivers.name: Samsung 47,000-Worker Strike Looming — Memory Supply Chain at Risk During Nvidia's Blackwell Ramp
drivers.linked: Samsung, STX, MU, HBM, NVDA, AVGO, memory supply
drivers.source: CNBC (Musk verdict article), Yahoo Finance live blog
drivers.detail: Samsung Electronics faces a 47,000-worker strike as South Korea's president urged a labor deal. The labour dispute is occurring as AI infrastructure demand has 'monopolised memory components' — Seagate -7% on contagion as the company uses Samsung chips in its data storage products. Micron -3% on sympathy. If the Samsung strike materialises, it would tighten HBM and DRAM supply at the worst possible moment: Nvidia needs Blackwell-grade memory for its data centre expansion and Apple needs advanced node SoCs for iPhone 18. This is the supply chain risk that is not yet in the headlines but is in the Seagate move.

drivers.name: G7 Finance Ministers in Paris — Rate Coordination Signal as Global Yields Surge
drivers.detail: G7 finance ministers met in Paris on Monday as global Treasury yields surged — Reuters confirmed the meeting. The agenda likely included the inflationary impact of the Iran-Hormuz closure on G7 economies, coordination on energy price relief, and the dollar's strength. The meeting's outcome was not yet reported but the backdrop — US 30Y at 5.13%, UK gilts elevated, EU yields rising — suggests the discussion was urgent. Any coordinated signal on rate paths or Iran energy policy would be a significant market catalyst.

risks.title: 10Y hits 5% before Warsh's June 17 — rate shock has momentum and no near-term catalyst to stop it
risks.desc: The 10Y is at 4.63% with the 30Y at 5.134% and the 2Y above 4%. The 10Y's year high was 4.48% — already surpassed. If Nvidia's Wednesday print disappoints OR Iran negotiations fail and Trump resumes military operations, the combined growth/inflation shock could push 10Y to 5% before June 17. A 5% 10Y would force Warsh to address the long-end dysfunction directly at his first meeting — potentially committing to rate cuts to reduce the fiscal premium, or QT tapering. Either outcome would be historically unusual.

risks.title: Samsung 47,000-worker strike — if declared, Blackwell ramp and Nvidia May 20 thesis are at risk
risks.desc: The Samsung strike is the session's most underappreciated risk. 47,000 workers would be the largest labour action in South Korean history for a tech firm. Samsung is the #2 HBM producer globally after SK Hynix. A strike would immediately constrain HBM availability for Nvidia's Blackwell products, AMD's MI series, and Apple's A-series. Seagate's -7% move on Monday was the early signal. If the strike is declared before Wednesday's Nvidia earnings, it introduces a direct supply-side uncertainty into Nvidia's Q2 guidance.

risks.title: Iran attack was only 'delayed' — Trump can restart military action within 24 hours if talks fail
risks.desc: Trump's announcement delayed the attack — it did not cancel it. The language was explicit: negotiations are 'serious' NOW. If Iran's amended terms are again rejected, the attack resumes. Brent's intraday move from $103 to $110+ and back to $108 on Monday shows the oil market's read: $8 of risk premium is still priced into every barrel. A resumed attack would immediately spike Brent above $115 and potentially $120.

risks.title: Nvidia May 20 — rate shock + Samsung risk = the bar for a 'sustaining beat' just rose sharply
risks.desc: Nvidia needs to report through: (1) a 25bp rate shock in 4 sessions (reducing present-value of growth premium), (2) Samsung strike uncertainty (supply chain for Blackwell), (3) H200 China deliveries still stalled (no revenue materialised from the approval), and (4) the Palantir/QCOM templates (clean beats at high multiples don't sustain). Data center >$45B + Q2 guide >$50B are now the floor, not the ceiling, for a positive market reaction.

risks.title: SpaceX IPO prospectus this week — 'second Musk stock' creates Tesla overhang
risks.desc: SpaceX plans to list on Nasdaq as soon as June 12, with the prospectus expected this week. Bloomberg noted: 'SpaceX IPO Adds Second Musk Stock. It's a Problem for Tesla.' SpaceX was valued at $1.25T after merging with xAI in February. A SpaceX IPO at $1.25T would dwarf Tesla's market cap — investors who want Musk exposure would shift from TSLA to SPCE/whatever the ticker is. Tesla's already complex narrative (Musk distraction, EV competition, autonomy) faces a new capital-allocation competitor.

strategies.title: Short TLT / Long TIPS — bear-steepener has momentum, 30Y at 5.13% is structural
strategies.body: The 30Y at 5.134% and 10Y at 4.63% confirm the stagflation trade is the dominant regime expression. Short TLT captures the continuing bear-steepener — Warsh June 17 with a 3.8% CPI backdrop makes a hawkish hold near-certain. Long TIPS captures both scenarios: if inflation stays elevated, TIPS win on real yield; if Iran resolves, TIPS hold while TLT rallies. The 10Y TIPS real yield at 2.1% is now compelling on an absolute basis. fedTransitionRisk at 82 is the highest indicator reading of the cycle.

strategies.title: Nvidia May 20 — position with sizing discipline, not maximum conviction
strategies.body: The rate shock (-25bps in 4 days), Samsung strike risk, H200 China delivery stall, and Palantir/QCOM templates all argue for reduced position size into the print. Nvidia needs data center >$45B and Q2 guide >$50B to sustain the multiple at current rates. A massive blowout (>$48B data center, >$53B Q2 guide) would overwhelm the rate headwinds. A clean but not blowout beat could trigger -7 to -10% on the day. Reduce pre-earnings exposure by 30-40%, reload on the guide if it's a supercycle confirmation.
